question: Which connective tissue layer wraps directly around an entire skeletal muscle?
explanation: The epimysium is the outer layer of connective tissue that wraps around the whole skeletal muscle. [learn more](BMP111_U3_T1#BMP111_U3_T1_h1)

question: What is the main job of fascicles inside a skeletal muscle?

options.A: They anchor the muscle tendons directly to the bone surface.
options.B: They group individual muscle fibers together within perimysium.
options.C: They store calcium ions needed for muscle shortening.
options.D: They produce ATP molecules for resting muscle tissue.

explanation: Fascicles are bundles of muscle fibers enclosed by the perimysium to help organize the muscle structure. [learn more](BMP111_U3_T1#BMP111_U3_T1_h1)

question: What is the name of the cell membrane of a skeletal muscle fiber?
explanation: The sarcolemma is the specialized cell membrane that surrounds a skeletal muscle fiber. [learn more](BMP111_U3_T1#BMP111_U3_T1_h2)

question: Where are calcium ions mainly stored inside a resting skeletal muscle fiber?
explanation: The sarcoplasmic reticulum stores calcium ions until a signal arrives telling the muscle to contract. [learn more](BMP111_U3_T1#BMP111_U3_T1_h2)

question: Which protein makes up thick myofilaments?
explanation: Thick filaments are built from bundled molecules of the protein myosin. [learn more](BMP111_U3_T1#BMP111_U3_T1_h3)

question: What marks the boundaries of a single sarcomere?

options.A: The region covered by the endomysium
options.B: The space inside a transverse tubule
options.C: The length of a single dark A-band
options.D: The distance between two adjacent Z-discs

explanation: A sarcomere is the functional unit of contraction, stretching from one Z-disc to the next. [learn more](BMP111_U3_T1#BMP111_U3_T1_h3)

question: Which change happens to the sarcomere when a muscle contracts?

options.B: The thin filaments shrink in size
options.D: The A-band significantly increases in length

explanation: As thin filaments slide inward, the Z-discs at the ends of the sarcomere are pulled closer together. [learn more](BMP111_U3_T1#BMP111_U3_T1_h4)

question: What happens to the actual length of thick and thin filaments when a muscle contracts?

options.A: They shorten significantly to pull the bone closer.
options.B: They stretch out to span the entire length of the muscle fiber.
options.C: They stay exactly the same length while sliding past each other.
options.D: They break apart and rebuild after every single movement.

explanation: Filaments do not change length during contraction; they simply slide past one another to shorten the sarcomere. [learn more](BMP111_U3_T1#BMP111_U3_T1_h4)

question: Which chemical messenger is released at the neuromuscular junction to stimulate muscle fibers?
explanation: Acetylcholine is released from motor neurons to cross over and stimulate the muscle fiber membrane. [learn more](BMP111_U3_T1#BMP111_U3_T1_h5)

question: What would happen if calcium ions could not bind to troponin inside a muscle fiber?

options.A: The thick filaments would instantly dissolve inside the sarcoplasm.
options.B: The muscle would undergo continuous spasms without stopping.
options.C: The nerve impulse would reverse direction back to the spinal cord.
options.D: The muscle would fail to contract because binding sites remain covered.

explanation: Calcium must bind to troponin to move tropomyosin and expose binding sites so contraction can happen. [learn more](BMP111_U3_T1#BMP111_U3_T1_h5)

question: Which molecule stores high-energy phosphate in muscle fibers for a quick supply of ATP?
explanation: Creatine phosphate quickly donates its phosphate group to refill ATP supplies at the start of exercise. [learn more](BMP111_U3_T1#BMP111_U3_T1_h6)

question: Why does anaerobic energy production lead to quicker muscle fatigue than aerobic respiration?

options.A: It immediately stops the release of acetylcholine from motor neurons.
options.B: It permanently destroys the Z-discs inside the contracting sarcomere.
options.C: It requires large amounts of oxygen that the bloodstream cannot supply.
options.D: It produces lactic acid and yields fewer total ATP molecules per glucose.

explanation: Anaerobic pathways produce less energy overall and create byproducts like lactic acid that lead to fatigue. [learn more](BMP111_U3_T1#BMP111_U3_T1_h6)
